2.text: THE following account of the Chukchee tribe contains chiefly the results

3.text: of my own observations, made during a protracted stay in the Kolyma district

4.text: from 1890 to 1898; and later during a journey to Kamchatka, Anadyr, and

5.text: the Chukchee Peninsula, in 1900-01. From 1895 to 1898 the work was

6.text: performed in connection with the Sibiryakoff Expedition, and part of the

7.text: material was published in Russian by the Imperial Academy of Sciences in

8.text: St. Petersburg.¹ The expedition of 1900-01 formed part of the Jesup North

9.text: Pacific Expedition. The collections made during this period are deposited in

10.text: the American Museum of Natural History.

11.text: On these journeys I visited nearly all parts of the country inhabited by

12.text: the Reindeer Chukchee, from central Kamchatka and the Upper Omolon to

13.text: Chaun Bay and Cape Chukotsky; but I saw only the maritime villages that

14.text: are located on the Pacific coast, between the mouth of the Anadyr and Indian

15.text: Point. These are inhabited by Chukchee and by Asiatic Eskimo.

16.text: In my protracted intercourse with the northern Reindeer camps I had

17.text: ample opportunity to see people from Arctic villages, and was able to obtain

18.text: a variety of information regarding their customs and manner of living.

19.text: The material life of the Reindeer Chukchee is quite uniform throughout

20.text: all the extensive territory occupied by their camps. The same may be said

21.text: of the maritime villages, which have exactly the same material culture, whether

22.text: they belong to Chukchee or to Eskimo tribes.

23.text: In order to avoid repetition, I have found it advisable to describe together

24.text: the main features of the material life of both Maritime Chukchee and Eskimo.
